idea: Localised distribution of Western research into Asian markets
buyer: Western research houses and boutique managers wanting Asian readership
pain: Their research is unread in Asia because nobody localises it
v1: Localise and distribute one house's research for a quarter
channel: Her research network and Asia contacts
verdict: Recurring and genuinely useful, but it is a service business dependent on someone else's product.

why.distribution: Research houses are semi-warm; the value depends on Asian distribution she must build.
why.demand: Inferred; most houses have decided Asia is not worth the effort.
why.fmf: Language and research literacy, but this is marketing and distribution rather than analysis.
why.defensibility: Translation and distribution are replicable services.
why.tailwind: Flat; cross-border research distribution faces compliance friction.
why.ceiling: £4k/mo x 5 houses = £240k, but five houses buying an unproven service is optimistic.

ceiling_arithmetic: £4k/mo x 5 houses = £240k gross less ~30% translation cost = £168k. Five retained houses is optimistic for a service nobody currently buys. Realistic: 1-2 = £34-67k.
carries: Genuinely recurring revenue and only five clients needed.
kills: Demand is unproven, margins are eaten by translation, and she owns none of the underlying product.
test: Ask three research houses whether Asian readership matters to them.
test_pass: They have tried and failed and would pay.
test_fail: They say Asia is not a priority.
